title: Piramal Glass unbottles smart manufacturing with Azure IoT and Microsoft AI
writeup:
## Case in point: Piramal Glass

## Piramal Glass provides glass packaging for pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and perfumery, and the specialty food and beverage industries. Through continued value addition, superior quality, and unmatched customer service, the company plans to become the world’s preferred supplier of glass packaging solutions with Microsoft Azure and AI solutions. 
In the era of digital transformation, adopting a new generation of technologies is imperative. In manufacturing, the competitive landscape and business models are changing at a rapid pace, and leaders are embracing digital-first strategies to stay ahead.

With end-to-end solutions in over 50 countries, offices and warehousing facilities in France, Germany, US, Brazil, India, UAE, United Kingdom, China, and Sri Lanka, Piramal Glass designs, produces, and decorates premium glass packaging material.

“Glass manufacturing is a complex industry with fixed costs and capacities that are therefore very sensitive to variations in demand. It was vital to optimize the operations to drive profitable growth and it was evident that Industry 4.0 was one of the key levers to achieve this,” says Vijay Shah, Director at Piramal Glass and Executive Director at Piramal Enterprises Ltd.

## Business need
Piramal Glass produces 1,375 tons of glass units per day across 60 production lines, all of which run on a 24/7 basis. Glass manufacturing involves various phases such as batch preparation, melting the raw materials in the furnace, bottle forming, treatments, various quality checks and packaging. In a single day, Piramal Glass produces dozens of bottle varieties across its production lines.

Glass containers are produced in a continuous manufacturing process which is very complex because of the numerous parameters that could impact quality. If the production lot witnesses higher rejections during quality control, they would usually be rectified in the next lot, resulting in production losses. 

In addition, the data was manually collected for each lot. Plant personnel would capture the data in paper-based logbooks, which proved difficult to analyze and did not provide timely insights to improve production. As a result, Piramal Glass was planning to improve production efficiency and minimize defects to transform its manufacturing process with technology. 

“Our vision is to become an insights-driven organization, where every employee can combine tradecraft and science in each bottle we make. Ultimately, we foresee the use of the digital technologies to be fundamental in our journey towards Industry 4.0,” says Poorav Sheth, Chief Digital Officer at Piramal Glass.

## Solution
An early adopter of technology, Piramal Glass decided to digitally transform its manufacturing operations by partnering with Microsoft for its Azure IoT platform. Piramal Glass took advantage of IoT to get real-time visibility into its manufacturing operations and analyze the defects at various stages. To facilitate this transformation, Websym, a Microsoft partner, brought in its plant monitoring system hosted on Microsoft Azure. Using Azure IoT Hub, data from equipment and high-speed production line sensors is pushed to the cloud for further analysis.

The first of its kind, a custom solution, Real Time Manufacturing Insights (RTMI), was developed on top of this platform to provide stage-wise losses, production reports, and quality control workflows, as well as role-specific key performance indicators (KPIs) on the personal computers and smartphones of plant personnel. Actionable alerts are sent through SMS, email, and push notifications whenever there is an anomaly detected or a drop in production efficiency. 

“On one hand, Microsoft Azure is continuing to emerge as the most sought-after cloud platform that’s allowing us to build cutting-edge solutions, bridging the value of the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge coming together. On the other hand, we’re really enthused by the vision of Piramal Glass to transform traditional processes in the digital-first world,” says Ashish Nene, CEO at Websym.

RTMI was piloted in three production lines in the Kosamba plant near Surat, Gujarat. Existing and retrofitted sensors were connected to the cloud with Azure IoT Hub and analyzed through RTMI. Since the benefits were evident early on, RTMI was scaled to 46 production lines across Piramal Glass plants in India, Sri Lanka, and the US, within a period of only six months.

This move eliminated paper logbooks, and data collection and analysis started happening in real time, with dashboards accessible on laptops, smartphones, and other devices. Plant personnel had easy access to production and defect metrics, quality control workflows, and role-specific KPIs. Alerts regarding production anomalies were immediately received through SMS, email, and push notifications. and the required corrective actions were taken immediately.

“We were impressed with the platform approach Microsoft has taken with Azure IoT and the industrial automation experience Websym brought to the table. We worked as a team where they also guided us on the kind of sensors and gateway devices we should use,” Sheth explains.

Currently, Piramal Glass is implementing AI and machine learning models using the Microsoft Cognitive Services platform to address the issues of anomaly detection, production efficiency, defect causality, and product quality for every production lot. The company is creating a unified view of all of its equipment and processes to create a digital twin of the manufacturing plant.

## Benefits
To date, Piramal Glass has analyzed over 200 million data points from the 4,000 sensors connected across its production units. The solution has enhanced the efficiency of plant managers in detecting anomalies in the process, monitoring key performance metrics, and making informed decisions in real time. 

RTMI has also reduced manual data gathering by 40 percent, resulting in a 25-percent improvement in employee productivity. The real-time feedback loop has led to a 1-percent improvement in production efficiency and 5-percent reduction in defects, which translates into better quality and enhanced predictability of delivery timelines for its customers.

title: Eureka Forbes delivers pure drops of water with Cloud and AI
writeup:
## Case in point: Eureka Forbes
“For us, even utilizing technology needs to stand true to our purpose—of making a positive difference to the lives of our customers and employees,” decrees Khushru Mistry, Chief Information Officer and Senior Vice President, Eureka Forbes, at the start of our conversation. 

My first brush with Eureka Forbes was more than two decades ago when as a 10-year-old, I saw a Eureka Forbes salesman demonstrate a vacuum cleaner and water purifier at home. Even today, in the age of single-click shopping and same-day home delivery, Eureka Forbes relies on its door-to-door direct sales model, employing more than 6,000 salespeople—one of the largest direct salesforces in Asia. 

This is the story of how Eureka Forbes is reinventing itself with cloud and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to stay ahead of the curve. 

Direct sales choreographed in the cloud 

“Ours is a cloud-oriented journey. That is one big decision we made. We realized, the strategy, from where we are right now to where we wish to be as a forward-looking brand, will only bear fruit if we adopt a cloud-first strategy,” Mistry says matter-of-factly. 

Part of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, Eureka Forbes is a multi-product, multi-channel organization, serving over 20 million customers across 1,500 cities in India and 35 countries worldwide. Its product portfolio encompasses water purification, vacuum cleaning, air purification, and home security solutions. 

Khushru Mistry, Chief Information Officer and Senior Vice President, Eureka Forbes is leading the company’s digital 
transformation by adopting to a cloud-first strategy with Microsoft Azure. “Whether people are buying a water purifier or any other consumer durable, they want the same experience as buying a pizza—it needs to be delivered to them quickly and in a transparent manner,” says Mistry. “However, when it comes to health and hygiene, and especially water, people want to know if they are drinking the right water. While many consumers are checking the prices online, we see a lot of them reaching out to our salespeople to understand which model suits them the best.”

To make their sales staff more productive, Eureka Forbes chose a cloud-based SaaS model for front-end apps that their salespeople can access directly on their smartphones. They wanted them to have access to granular insights like water quality and the right product to sell in real-time. The company has mapped over 10,400 PIN codes in the country for its water quality and made it available to its sales force.

“In many cases, we know the quality of water at a building level in which customers use our products. We provide this information to our salespeople, so they can suggest the right product to customers,” adds Mistry.

With cold door-to-door visits becoming restricted in gated communities, the company implemented [Dynamics 365](https://dynamics.microsoft.com/en-in/) on the back-end to provide digital leads and customer insights to drive sales effectiveness.

“Before getting to the design table, we went to the grass roots. The Microsoft team accompanied Euro Champs in door-to-door sales to observe and understand the challenges they were facing,” says Samik Roy, Country Head, Microsoft Modern Workplace, Microsoft India.

“We consolidated the seven different CRM systems we had into one and it runs on Dynamics 365. We had a significant amount of data both from India and abroad, and we are already seeing a positive return on investment,” reveals Mistry. “Going forward, we’ll be able to gain deeper insights, utilizing advanced analytics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to help us understand our customers better.”

“As a 100% SaaS solution, Microsoft Dynamics 365’s USP is its seamless integration with Azure cloud services, Office 365 and LinkedIn. This helps Eureka Forbes accelerate their digital transformation journey. AI, Rich Analytics and ML fuels the CRM application natively, thus enabling the end user to have a personalized conversation with the company. All of these (Dynamics 365, Office 365, Azure, AI, Analytics, and ML) solutions jointly enhance the efficiency and productivity of every person in the value chain,” Roy adds.

While the salespeople were getting good leads and customer insights to make a convincing sales pitch, there was one more hurdle. The company’s back-end SAP system that supported planning, procurement, production, sales, and payroll management, was still hosted on-premise and couldn’t handle peak workloads. As a sales-oriented organization, the agility of the sales systems is an essential determinant of its business efficiency.

With [SAP on Azure](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/solutions/sap/), Eureka Forbes’ tech backbone can now flex on demand. It has also given the leadership visibility on month-on-month trends that helps them plan their sales cycle better.

Delivering personalized water 

With the front-end and back-end systems for the sales function migrated on to Microsoft Azure, Eureka Forbes is also planning to launch a slew of services to improve its customer experience.

But this is just the beginning. Eureka Forbes now has its eyes set on what can be considered the holy grail of water purification systems—customizing the taste of water depending on the user’s preference.

“Whether you realize it or not, water has a taste, and people don’t drink water if they don’t like its taste. At the end of the day, these features are all about interfacing with our customers and improving their lives. We want to ensure people drink pure water and they drink enough water,” Mistry says.

title: ABB keeps the lights on with AI-based workforce management software
writeup:
## Case in point: ABB Group
Utilities and other asset-based businesses rely on ABB software to efficiently manage their assets and field workforces at a time when asset infrastructures are aging and budgets are tight. ABB is transforming its workforce management applications into software as a service (SaaS) offerings using Microsoft Azure. The newest product, ABB Ability Ellipse Workforce Management (WFM), mobilizes maintenance, inspection, and outage work, which delivers greater worker efficiency, vast scalability, continuous innovation, and lower costs.

Let’s face it, we all take power and electricity for granted. For as long as we’ve all known, it’s been there for us—always on, always strong. It’s in the background lighting our way, powering our homes, enabling our ever-growing digital lifestyle.

But, it’s more fragile than we think. A strong gust of wind, a broken branch, simple human error, and our lives are suddenly interrupted. Extreme weather events, such as high winds, flooding, and extreme heat, can force power outages, plunging modern cities into darkness.

ABB works hard to keep the darkness at bay. The Zurich, Switzerland–based engineering giant makes equipment used in all phases of power generation, distribution, and transmission—from room-sized transformers and massive switchgears to capacitors and transmission systems.

Through its Enterprise Software group, ABB also makes software that helps asset-intensive businesses such as utilities address inspection, maintenance, and outage work, and mobilize their workforces to execute work efficiently. For 20 years, utilities in electric, gas, water, and other verticals have used ABB workforce management software to get the right technician with the right skills to the right place at the right time—to keep their assets functioning optimally. Hundreds of customers rely on ABB software to make their assets and their field workforces more productive and efficient.

The company’s marque WFM application is ABB Ability Ellipse Workforce Management (WFM), introduced in December 2017. It empowers service technicians to navigate the challenges of performing routine or complex inspections and maintenance work using world-class mobility. It is an evolution of the ABB on-premises workforce management solution that thousands of mobile technicians and dispatchers rely on every day to solve their toughest field challenges. In fact, ABB data shows that customers using the software have increased field productivity by 15 to 25 percent, decreased their drive time between sites by 10 percent, and improved customer satisfaction by 20 percent.

## Look to the cloud to stay ahead of customer needs
When ABB set out to develop ABB Ability Ellipse WFM, it had a long list of customer requests: hands-free interaction so that field technicians wouldn’t need to remove their gloves to enter data, easy connectivity to home-office staff for impromptu consultation and assistance, an “evergreen” cloud-based deployment model that eliminated on-premises software upgrades, and more scalability for utilities and other asset-intensive companies that need to manage large-scale field workforces.

“Our customers’ businesses are evolving,” says James Pierre-Noel, Senior Director of Product Management at ABB Enterprise Software. “Many utilities have aging infrastructures, which changes the way they maintain and inspect their gear. An asset that’s 2 years old doesn’t need much inspection, but a 25-year-old transformer requires a lot more attention. Most utilities have budget only to replace 5 percent of their infrastructure in any given year, so they want to empower their field workforce to do more effective maintenance on these assets.”

ABB decided that the cloud offered the fastest path to meeting customers’ urgent needs. “The innovation cycle moves very quickly today—we want to set the pace by offering our customers advances like wearable technology that deliver value beyond what competitors offer,” Pierre-Noel says. “We can adopt new technology and innovate faster in the cloud.”

ABB Ability, the unique ABB integrated industrial internet platform that uses [Microsoft Azure](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/), serves as the backbone for ABB Ability Workforce Management. The platform creates an open, globally available digital-industrial ecosystem for customers, partners, suppliers, and developers and takes full advantage of Azure cybersecurity, artificial intelligence (AI), and core services, such as [Azure IoT solution accelerators](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/features/iot-accelerators/) and [Cortana Intelligence](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/overview/ai-platform/). This allows ABB customers to capitalize on insights gathered at every level, from device to system, enterprise, and cloud.

“We appreciate that Azure is available in 32 regions around the globe, with plans for more, because we have customers in just about every country of the world,” says Pierre-Noel. “It’s critical that we partner with a company that can follow our business wherever we go.”

Pierre-Noel’s team used Azure platform as a service (PaaS) offerings, such as [Azure SQL Database](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/sql-database/), [Azure Service Bus](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/service-bus/), and [Azure Service Fabric](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/service-fabric/), to drive Ability Ellipse WFM using a microservices-based architecture. The team further converted Ability Ellipse WFM into a software as a service (SaaS) offering, eliminating the need for customers to install it on-premises.

ABB uses an [Azure Cognitive Search](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/search/)–based engine for fast, easy searching through operational data on control room dashboards. It uses the [Logic Apps](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/logic-apps/) feature of [Azure App Service](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/app-service/) to connect Ellipse WFM to other enterprise systems, such as SAP and Maximo. And it uses [Azure Application Insights](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/application-insights/) and [Azure Log Analytics](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/log-analytics/) to monitor system health and provide dashboards and alerts. Soon, ABB will use [Microsoft Cognitive Services](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/cognitive-services/), [Azure Machine Learning](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/machine-learning-services/), and [Azure Bot Service](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/bot-service/) to add chatbots, predictive analytics, and other AI capabilities to Ellipse WFM.

“We’re excited to develop software in the cloud. It allows us to deliver faster to market and gives us the flexibility to innovate using a modern architecture,” Pierre-Noel says. “A SaaS model enables us to deliver outstanding infrastructure reliability and performance, which in turn gives our customers the confidence to run their businesses on our infrastructure. Microsoft has really helped us navigate any concerns about moving to the cloud.”

## Increase worker productivity 
ABB Ability Ellipse WFM includes modern features that help field maintenance staff work more efficiently and safely. It incorporates hands-free operation and voice interactivity, which makes it easier for field technicians to keep both hands available for work in situations where holding a device simply isn’t feasible. For example, inspections while hanging 10 meters in the air off the side of an electrical tower become easier and safer to execute.  

Ellipse WFM is part of ABB Connected Asset Lifecycle Management, which allows a work order to move through the Ellipse Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), Asset Performance Management (APM), and Workforce Management (WFM) modules, allowing customers to do condition-based monitoring of assets. This is a vast improvement over the time-based asset management employed by many utilities today. 

In addition to hands-free functionality using a wearable device, Ellipse WFM features innovations, such as the ability to stream live video to the back office for virtual assistance and the ability to self-dispatch work to fill idle time, all of which lets a field force be more productive.   

Soon, through the use of Cognitive Services, a technician will be able to say to Ellipse WFM, “I see a transformer leak; create a service order,” and the software will do so. And on the ABB roadmap is the ability for Ellipse WFM to incorporate more Cognitive Services like image recognition into the software’s standard offering. These are only some of the many planned innovations coming in the near future to Ellipse WFM.

“It’s an exciting time, because with Ellipse WFM we are finding new ways to disrupt the market and change the way customers think about workforce management,” Pierre-Noel says.

## Gain vast scalability, drip-feed improvement
The product’s cloud and microservices–based architecture delivers many benefits. ABB considers scalability one of the most important. “With Azure, we can scale Ellipse WFM to serve tens of thousands of users,” Pierre-Noel says.

Elastic scalability is especially valuable when major storms hit and utilities call in hundreds of extra service technicians to help restore power. With Ellipse WFM in the hands of all those technicians, utilities will have much better, real-time information about what’s going on in the field. This helps them give end customers and stakeholders, such as local and state governments, a sense of when services will be restored, be they electric, gas, or water.

Offering Ellipse WFM as a SaaS product eliminates big, expensive product upgrades. Today, ABB can “drip-feed” a steady stream of innovation to customers through an evergreen software model. “As we develop new functionality, we can push it out to customers, get their feedback, and create a continuous and iterative cycle of improvement,” Pierre-Noel says.

ABB plans to enhance Ellipse WFM with chat bots that prompt technicians for specific answers and essentially talk them through a service procedure. The company might also take advantage of in-device cameras to monitor technicians’ movements, so that Ellipse WFM can issue safety warnings, advice, and guidance.

“In Azure, we have a rich menu of services that we can use to make our workforce management solution smarter so field technicians are more productive,” Pierre-Noel says. “Partnering with Microsoft means we can rely on their resources to deliver the infrastructure needed to support our vision, and they bring the added benefit of making integration to our product seamless.”

## Reduce costs, reach smaller customers
Because Ellipse WFM is a SaaS solution, it’s affordable for thousands of smaller utilities around the world that can‘t afford enterprise workforce management solutions. “Our focus is bringing down total cost of ownership for our customers, and Azure helps us do that,” says Pierre-Noel. “Instead of spending millions of dollars a year to run a solution on-premises, our customers spend a flat amount per user per year for Ellipse WFM. We’re greatly expanding our market while helping thousands more utilities manage their mobile workforces more efficiently.”

By helping customers put the right technician with the right skills and tools in the right place at the right time, ABB helps customers with all types of networks keep their assets running optimally—and keep the lights on.

title: Oil and gas experts use machine learning to deploy predictive analytics at the edge
writeup:
## Case in point: Schneider Electric
For companies with connected assets distributed across a country or around the world, edge analytics makes remote asset management easier by putting application logic onsite. However, some businesses may have remote assets without easy access to the cloud, and they may be reluctant to send data outside their own networks. Schneider Electric is out to solve that challenge for the oil and gas industry. The company has pushed edge solutions into new, predictive realms with the help of [Azure Machine Learning](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/machine-learning/) and [Azure IoT Edge](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/campaigns/iot-edge/).

The Internet of Things (IoT) has brought remote monitoring and control to a vast array of devices, from building thermostats to retention pond spillways to oil and gas artificial lift pumps. IoT connectivity can facilitate routine adjustments to settings or performance, or it can enable shutdown of a device that is failing. However, once the device reaches an abnormal operating condition, it may be too late to maintain efficiency, prevent damage, or avoid a dangerous situation. But what if it were possible to embed intelligence at the network edge—where IoT devices reside—that could predict abnormal operating conditions before they happen and take preventive action?

## New ways to manage remote assets
Headquartered in Paris, France, Schneider Electric is a leader in the digital transformation of energy management and automation. The company’s commitment to innovation and sustainable development in the oil and gas industry drives the creation of leading-edge tools for monitoring and managing resource production and consumption. Schneider uses EcoStruxure—its IoT-enabled, plug-and-play, open-architecture platform—as a hub for collaborating across its ecosystem of partners to deliver real-time control and operational efficiency.

Schneider Electric solutions play a key role for oil and gas companies that may have thousands of pumps spread over a large geographic area. For these companies, efficiently managing all of the pumps is key to business success. “With the volatility of oil prices, producers are under tremendous pressure to shrink production costs and increase efficiency,” says Fahd Saghir, Industry Solutions Manager (Upstream O&G) for Schneider Electric. “We provide tools that help them do that.”

The Realift Rod Pump Control is one such Schneider Electric solution. Rod pumps are the iconic pivoting pumps that dot oil fields around the world. Using Realift, companies can monitor and configure pump settings and operations remotely, only sending personnel onsite when necessary for repair or maintenance when Realift indicates that something has gone wrong.

But Schneider Electric was interested in enhancing Realift to do more than just respond to real-time situations. The company wanted to give it the ability to predict problems so they can be averted before a fault occurs and damage is done. “If you look at most of the controllers that exist in the market today, they are reactive, looking at what is happening now and responding accordingly,” says Helenio Gilabert, Director for SCADA and Telemetry at Schneider Electric. “We want to be proactive and include predictive analytics at the edge. It’s a real game changer.”

## From reactive to proactive
The Schneider Electric development team investigated ways to incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning into Realift to add that predictive capability. The company had worked with Microsoft Azure in the past, so when it came time to incorporate AI into Realift, the team saw [Azure Machine Learning](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/machine-learning/) and [Azure IoT Edge](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/campaigns/iot-edge/) as the right tools for the job.

“Azure Machine Learning gave us the powerful intelligence we need, as well as flexible model management capabilities,” says Matt Boujonnier, Analytics Application Architect for Schneider Electric. “And IoT Edge provided an easy way to package and deploy our Machine Learning applications. Traditionally, machine learning is something that has only run in the cloud, but for many IoT scenarios that isn’t good enough, because you want to run your application as close as possible to any events. Now we have the flexibility to run it in the cloud or at the edge—wherever we need it to be.”

Using Machine Learning gives Realift the ability to analyze readings from various elements of the rod pump mechanism and sense patterns that indicate a possible impending mechanical failure or a deviation from the pump’s optimal operating conditions. In that case, the controller can modify the operating parameters of the pump to avoid or mitigate the impact of the unexpected changes. Or, if necessary, it can shut down the pump before any damage occurs and notify the company that repairs are necessary—protecting the machinery, and preventing potential environmental damage.

## A safer, more efficient workplace
The deployment of predictive models to edge devices helps Schneider Electric customers meet business goals, safeguard their valuable industrial assets, protect the environment, and boost workplace safety.

“One clear business benefit is operator efficiency,” says Saghir. “By proactively identifying pump problems through edge analytics, companies reduce unplanned downtime, which decreases costs, increases production, and increases the agility of maintenance services."

Adds Gilabert, "The majority of industry accidents don’t happen at the well site, they happen when personnel are driving between sites. By eliminating the need for many site visits, we reduce those accidents.”

In addition to reducing or avoiding unwanted communication between remote assets and central systems, edge analytics can boost the speed at which important decisions happen. “In some critical systems or critical processes—whether at an oil pump or in a manufacturing plant—you may have to make a decision in a matter of milliseconds, and someone’s life could be at stake,” says Boujonnier. “By building machine learning algorithms into our applications and deploying analytics at the edge, we reduce any communication latency to the cloud or a central system, and that critical decision can happen right away.”

title:
Automation of battery formation management process for
a large scale lead-acid battery manufacturer in India
writeup:
## About Utthunga

## The challenge faced by customer

Battery formation is a critical process in the battery manufacturing process, which
directly affects battery quality. A VRLA Battery Manufacturer was looking for digitization
of their formation process as the manual methods were posing challenges in acquisition,
recording and storing of the formation data. Accuracy, consistency and timely capturing
of data was required and data had to be retained for many years for compliance and
failure analysis.

## Scope of work

Utthunga clearly understood the requirement by interacting with the Operators and
understanding the entire formation process. Utthunga came up with a solution having
Tablet based application, which would be used, by the operators and the Server to
maintain the history data and enable reports. Tablet was interfaced with a Hardware
module to interface with the Voltage probes and Current clamp meter.

## Solutions and services provided by utthunga

## The Approach

Utthunga team designed a Tablet based solution with probes to measure voltage and
current for various intervals in charging & discharging cycles. The application was
integrated with Bluetooth enabled QR Code Scanner to track individual batteries.

The time stamping of the data makes it accurate with respect to key battery parameters
Post data collection the data is electronically transferred to the standard format
provided by manufacturer and to a central database where it is stored. Tablet Assisted
process for operators including Alarms and Multiple devices are supported and also
formation process can be continued from one device to the other
Javelin provides central access for all the records and reports.

## Technology and Methodology used:

GM-100: It is a hand-held device designed to be used by the operators during the
battery formation process. The hand-held device enables the user to measure the
Bank/ Battery voltage and current during the formation process through wireless
(Bluetooth enabled) Voltage/Current clamp meter. Then the data is pushed to the
centralized server. GM-100 is a convenient solution, which reduces the time, and effort
needed to record formation data and ensures high accuracy at the same time. In case
the server goes down, the hand-held device will continue to operate in ‘Island Mode’.
This means, the end user without any problem can use the device and the data will be
stored locally on the device. When the server come up, the data gets synced to the
server.

Javelin: All the parameters measured by the device are logged and uploaded
instantaneously to the centralized IIOT platform called Javelin. System configuration,
User management, Reports creation is done in Javelin. 

## Implementation and specific learnings

GM-100 field device and Javelin IIoT application are two of our important products in
battery formation solution. GM-100 consists of a Windows Tablet in a safe casing with
ports for connecting current and voltage meters. Javelin IIoT application has a dashboard
with formation stage summary, analytics and provides necessary reports to download.

## Benefits to the customer

- 100% accuracy of collected data and timely data capture suitable for Audits.

- Digitization of the Formation process improved the efficiency by reducing the personnel cost by 50%.

- No manual entry into formation log sheet, which prevents human errors improving the battery quality.

- Historical data maintained for many years with download option.

title: Ship Fuel Monitoring System for Ship Management Services Company

## About Utthunga

## The Client

Our client is a major Ship Management Services company They presently manage
around 40 vessels for ship owners from Japan, Singapore, Greece, Isle of Man and
Croatia. Their offices are located in Singapore, Norway, India, Philippines and
Vietnam with representatives in China and Japan as well. Their complete range of
ship management involves managing most of the ships complete life cycle, from
allocation of blueprint, through construction, operational life, dry-docking, midlife
modernization, life extensions and ultimately recycling.

## Challenge Faced by the Customer

The Ship Management Services Company had problems in maintaining the
inventory of the fuel consumption in their ships/vessels. There was high
probability of fuel consumption data erroneously being entered by the ship
attendants. The accuracy in fuel consumption data was also missing. Hence, the
customer wanted to track the consumption of fuel in an automated manner.

## Scope of Work

Based on the client’s requirements, Utthunga suggested that a customized
uConnect is required that is basically an edge device/gateway used for any IoT
platform to connect to field devices and other industrial assets. The device is fixed
to the main and auxiliary engines to read data from the flow meters. uConnect
edge application then processes the data and publishes it securely to a web
server.

## Solutions & Services Provided by Utthunga

The basic approach and implementation methodology used by Utthunga to
resolve the client’s challenge is as follows.

## Approach

Utthunga team worked on the uConnect device to meet the customer
requirements with below features:

- Tamper proof data acquisition and storage

- Fuel consumption calculation (for different fuel types) logic based on data
collected from different flow meters

- Secure data transmission via Restful webserver

- In-device portal to access flow consumption in the ship

- Audit Trails

- Publishing the data to a centralized server for analysis and reports

## Technology and Methodology Used

- uConnect / Edge Device

- Collects fuel flow reading from flow meters over MODBUS

- Captures analog, digital input, RPM data

- Captures marine parameters

- GPS Signals

- Speed

- Gyro

- Anemometer readings

- Monitors dual fuel types

- HSFO

- LSGO

- Analytics application running on the edge device

- Fuel consumption is calculated periodically and posted to cloud server for offshore monitoring

- Data posted in XML format using REST API

- Store and forward in case of network dis-connectivity

## Implementation

- The customized uConnect edge device was installed in 20 ships and data is continuously acquired and sent to a centralized server

- One-click software updates to the edge device is through a portable pen
drive which is an easy, simple and mobile way for ship maintenance.

## Benefits to the customer

- Customer has complete fuel ledger with transparency in fuel stock

- Ship movement and all critical parameters are monitored by the stake holders

- Centralized server to access the data from all the ships.

title: Larsen & Toubro Construction unlocks business value with a connected equipment platform powered by Microsoft Azure IoT and AI
writeup:
## Case in point: L & T construction

Just boarded a flight from a major Indian airport? Most likely, the complete airport infrastructure was built by [Larsen & Toubro (L&T) Construction](https://www.lntecc.com/). An integral part of L&T Group, L&T Construction is a USD21 billion technology, engineering, and construction conglomerate.

Driving down a national highway in India or taking a metro ride for a quick commute? It’s quite likely that these are successfully executed projects by L&T Construction. The Statue of Unity, the world’s tallest statue, was built in record time under challenging circumstances by L&T Construction.

Ranked among the top 15 global contractors by [Engineering News Review](https://www.lntecc.com/homepage/common/corpawards.html), L&T Construction is India’s largest construction company. It designs and builds some of the largest construction projects across the globe, spanning airports, residential buildings, factories, highways, railways, metros, special bridges, dams, infrastructure for power transmission & distribution, renewable energy plants, water and effluent treatment plants, and smart cities.

L&T Construction is among the pioneers spearheading digital transformation in the global construction industry through ”Digital @ Construction,” a program that focuses on accelerating project progress, enhancing operational efficiencies, and enabling data-driven decision making. As a part of this transformation program, L&T Construction has developed and deployed cutting-edge digital solutions and platforms across the construction value chain.

One such key platform that is deployed at scale is Asset Insight, a connected equipment platform that takes advantage of Microsoft Azure IoT and AI.

## Equipment fleet of L&T Construction 

L&T Construction owns, operates, and maintains more than 35,000 pieces of equipment at over 450 project sites spread across the globe. This constitutes a variety of equipment, like tower cranes, concrete batching plants, motor graders, pavers, weighbridges, power generators, and piling rigs. This equipment is sourced from more than 100 original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).

“Construction progress has a very high dependence on ensuring availability, proper utilization, and optimum productivity of the construction equipment fleet. Achieving this requires the ability to acquire, analyze, and derive business insights based on equipment operational data, health, location, utilization, production data, and take business decisions based on the insights derived—all in real time,” explains Anantha Sayana, Chief Digital Officer at L&T Group.

## Asset Insight—L&T’s connected equipment platform

In one of L&T Construction’s remote monitoring cells, an engineer analyzes equipment productivity versus internal hiring charges to decide on hiring of concrete batching plants. Another engineer zooms into the dashboard of a motor grader operating thousands of kilometers away to analyze and understand utilization and operating patterns. 

Automated alerts generated by the connected weighbridges use advanced analytics and computer vision to help the operating personnel identify weighment anomalies. Insights derived from granular, real-time data have transformed equipment lifecycle management at L&T Construction. 

“Asset Insight, our connected equipment platform that capitalizes on industrial IoT, advanced analytics, machine learning, and computer vision, has helped us create an ecosystem of connected products and services. As of today, more than 11,000 construction equipment across 450 sites are connected to the Asset Insight platform, streaming real-time data and information about location, utilization, production, operational, and health parameters. Insights derived from the Asset Insight platform have enabled us to increase equipment productivity, enhance capacity utilization, right-size assets, improve fuel efficiency, and reduce capital expenditure,” says Balajikasiram S, Head – Digital at L&T Construction.

## The Azure PaaS advantage

The Asset Insight platform was built using several [Azure platform as a service](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/overview/what-is-paas/) (PaaS) components, namely, [Azure IoT Hub](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/overview/what-is-paas/), [Stream Analytics](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/services/stream-analytics/), [Blob Storage](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/services/storage/blobs/), [HDInsight](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/services/hdinsight/), [Azure Cosmos DB](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/try/cosmosdb/), [Azure SQL Database](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/services/sql-database/), [App Service](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/services/app-service/), and [Microsoft Power BI](https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/).

There are several advantages to these PaaS components. For example, Azure IoT Hub helps in seamless ingestion of telemetry data from thousands of field IoT gateways that are fitted on construction equipment. Stream Analytics creates robust streaming data pipelines flowing into Blob Storage. HDInsight provides enterprise-grade service for analytics, ranging from time series to machine learning that helps derive insights on equipment availability, utilization patterns, fuel efficiency, and productivity. And finally, business users consume insights using intuitive role-based dashboards developed with Power BI. 

Armed with these insights, managers at L&T Construction can take various tangible actions, such as undertaking specific maintenance activities to improve equipment availability, and right-sizing equipment based on project requirements and past usage data. Other actions include releasing unused and underutilized equipment from construction sites and streamlining construction processes to improve productivity. Managers can provide operator training to facilitate proper equipment operation, improve productivity, and reduce equipment idling. In addition, they can share equipment output such as concrete produced by batching plants across multiple site locations, and dispense fuel based on equipment usage data.

“Azure IoT gives us real-time visibility into the operations at our project sites and enhances our ability to manage projects. We are delighted that we can provide our operating managers with accurate information and real-time insights on how their machines are performing. These specific insights have enabled our managers to take business decisions that have already given us significant operational benefits,” adds Sayana. 

“Our partnership with Microsoft augments our capability to unlock unparalleled efficiencies, intelligence, and productivity with the help of innovations in the cloud, IoT, and Artificial Intelligence,” concludes S N Subrahmanyan, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director at L&T Group.

title: Eureka Forbes’ Eureka Moment on the Cloud – Efficiencies and Agility Unlocked with Microsoft Azure
writeup:
## Case in point: Eureka Forbes Limited

## In the wake of increasing competition and rising demand for modernization, leading players in the consumer goods industry race to create a sustainable competitive edge. Much of the differentiation is driven through process automation, operational efficiencies to drive economies at scale, and creation of customer delight through empowered employees. One such front-runner in this transformation landscape is [Eureka Forbes Limited](https://www.eurekaforbes.com/), India’s leading health and hygiene brand - powered by Microsoft Azure.

Part of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, Eureka Forbes is a multi-product, multichannel organization, serving over 20 million customers across 1,500 cities in India and 40 countries worldwide. Its product portfolio encompasses water purification, vacuum cleaning, air purification, and home security solutions. The company safeguards the productivity of its 7,800-plus employees and meets the demands of millions of external consumers through Microsoft Azure.

## Encountering downtimes

More than 7,800 employees of Eureka Forbes utilize front-end sales force automation mobile apps which interface to back-end SAP systems. The SAP system supports planning, procurement, production, sales, and payroll management. Four key SAP applications are used across processes: SAP ERP Central Component (ECC), SAP Customer Relationship Management (CRM), SAP Business Warehouse (BW), and SAP Enterprise Portal (EP). On SAP ECC, for instance, the company handles approximately 140,000 sales orders, 100,000 invoices, and 65,000 purchase orders per month. 

Since most sales usually occurred close to the end of the month, the company’s legacy systems struggled to handle the 2.5 to 3x peak workloads. Unable to conduct high-volume, concurrent transactions, Eureka Forbes faced slow response, affecting day-to-day activities like accessing stock data, generating reports, and filing Goods and Services Tax (GST). The organization faced operational complexities with its on-premises datacenters.

“A key issue we used to face with IBM AIX, despite its robust nature, was with the interlinking of versions of SAP development, quality assurance (QA), and production systems as sequential operations. Every version upgrade required us to set aside around 72 hours for data backup and QA,” says Khushru Mistry, Chief Information Officer and Senior Vice President at Eureka Forbes. This timeline made it impossible for the company to introduce improvements without impacting the existing system and bringing everything to a standstill. 

 With its on-premises IT systems nearing the end of life, the company decided to migrate its Tier-1 payload (SAP) into the cloud.

## Upgrading uptime with Azure

To take advantage of technology as a strategic growth driver, Eureka Forbes was looking for an IT platform that would scale up and be flexible enough to respond to seasonal fluctuations on demand. It was weighing options to optimize IT costs and datacenter infrastructure, while also planning ahead to employ AI and IoT to enhance business processes. 

To accelerate the performance of four core applications, the company migrated its on-premises SAP with Oracle database (AIX) systems to SAP with Oracle (Oracle Linux) on Microsoft Azure. The migration included implementation of Azure services, such as [Azure Backup](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/services/backup/?&OCID=AID719810_SEM_E60xQ30O&lnkd=Bing_Azure_Brand&msclkid=332e223c5ad51bc5be507f2d5f8ef154&dclid=CLa2083PguMCFZWBcAod_WcD3A) to have continuous real-time backup of data; sound data management mechanism with near-zero downtime with [Disaster Recovery options](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/solutions/disaster-recovery/?&OCID=AID719810_SEM_QJloszcC&lnkd=Bing_Azure_Brand&msclkid=475bfe7bbc9916d3cf54a36ab96afeed&dclid=COnW1JLQguMCFVaGjwodHQsNiA), alongside [Azure Express Route](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/expressroute/) for high reliability and connectivity with low latency; and [Azure Site Recovery](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/site-recovery/) for replicating non-SAP systems. This is a process that is currently underway.

Post-migration, Eureka Forbes is taking advantage of other services like [Logic Apps](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/logic-apps/), which is integrated with SAP system to send e-invoices to business users; [Traffic Analytics](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/traffic-analytics); and [Network Watcher](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/network-watcher/) to monitor network traffic. 

“With our on-premises systems, data replication used to take up to three hours, but after moving to Azure, it takes under 15 minutes, making our transactions more seamless than ever,” remarks Mistry. “ Adding to this, the trusted ecosystem of Microsoft’s cloud partners sealed the deal for us.”

## Pure ‘drops of gain’ 

Eureka Forbes recorded significant performance improvements in its daily operations, especially during peak times. After migrating its core SAP applications to Azure, the dynamic horizontal and vertical scaling allowed sales personnel to focus on meeting monthly targets instead of processing them.

“We’re now easily generating about 150,000 invoices and catering to around 1,000,000 service orders per month in a timely manner - ultimately helping us better serve our customers with faster responses,” explains Mistry.

While employees involved in the operations benefited from quick loading of required data with no latency, application developers benefited from lightning-fast synchronization of Development, QA, and Production modules in the cloud. 

“What used to take close to three full days, now just takes under 60 minutes on Azure,” concludes Mistry.

Using in-memory computing capabilities, drag-and-drop features, and higher storage, Eureka Forbes envisions a future-ready environment - today.

Today, M&M is a global conglomerate of more than 150 companies and a USD 20.7 billion group with business presence in 100-plus countries. With R&D facilities across 13 countries and 63 manufacturing facilities globally, the group employs more than 250,000 employees. It operates in key industries that form the foundation of every modern economy, including aerospace and defense, aftermarket, agribusiness, automotive, farm equipment, two-wheelers, financial services, hospitality, information technology, partners, and real estate. 

The enterprise is spearheading industries and paving new paths, as the world’s largest tractor company by volume, India’s largest electric vehicle maker, and one of the country’s largest utility vehicle manufacturers. 

## Rising beyond barriers 

Across its diverse verticals and geographical spread, M&M is fueled by its ‘Rise’ philosophy. “The Rise credo is about accepting no limits, alternative thinking, and driving positive change—the three pillars,” explains Anand Mahindra, Chairman at Mahindra Group. “Whether in services or in manufacturing, the trick is to stay ahead of the curve. I believe we should not wait to be disrupted—we should become disruptors ourselves,” he adds. 

Continued innovation driven by seamless collaboration between stakeholders was, therefore, a business imperative.

For the teams at M&M, email was the primary mode of communication. But a constant influx of emails hampered productivity. Although multiple chat-based platforms were being used across the enterprise, the disparate array of tools made collaboration challenging. Connectivity issues, two-way communication with the leadership team, and employee engagement through social activities were other hurdles that the company faced. 

“We wanted our people to embrace a simple collaboration tool that could help break down silos between teams and facilitate information exchange on the go. We also wanted to reduce email and induce a shift towards simplicity,” says Bishwanath Ghosh, CIO Enterprise & Corporate Functions at M&M. Well acquainted with the versatility and security of [Microsoft Office 365](https://www.office.com/) and [Skype for Business](https://www.skype.com/en/business/), [Microsoft Teams](https://www.microsoft.com/en-in/microsoft-365/microsoft-teams/group-chat-software) was the company’s go-to choice. Under the leadership of Mr. Ghosh, an adoption team was appointed to lead this effort enterprise wide, coined as mBaarish [Pour of Knowledge at M&M].

## Upgrading to a best-in-class collaboration platform

Today, Teams is the shared workspace of more than 30,000 employees* of M&M. Teams is also used at other entities in Mahindra Group, such as Tech Mahindra and Mahindra Holidays. These are not covered in this case-study.

“On Teams, we can bring everyone together so they can jointly work on projects, share ideas, and interact from anywhere. In a short span, the simplicity and ease of use of Teams have made it our central communication and collaboration platform,” explains Murlidhar Rao, General Manager Datacenter Operations at M&M. 

Other key benefits include: 

- Seamless two-way communication: When remote working became the norm due to COVID-19, employees could continue to engage with colleagues and business partners seamlessly. The group chats on Teams greatly eased communication, as it takes just a few clicks to set up a quick huddle or video conferences with the dealer network.In fact, teams have collaborated in 3,50,000 virtual meetings over a span of 40 days. What’s more, the leadership team, including the managing director, has been effectively disseminating corporate communication through 80-plus live events.

- 360-degree engagement: For the HR teams, the platform has opened up a whole new way of employee engagement. From musical events to Zumba classes, varied activities are helping everyone catch up and keep the fun alive virtually—even after office hours.

- Cloud-powered collaboration and enterprise-grade security: The effective compatibility of day-to-day Office 365 tools and shared documents on [OneDrive](https://www.microsoft.com/en-in/microsoft-365/onedrive/online-cloud-storage) simplifies remote collaboration with assured security. In the strategy team, which deals with business-critical data, the silo approach is maintained. “We create different channels within Teams to keep sensitive information in silos. We also keep uploading documents and work together. This helps in version control because there is no need for a flurry of emails with revised versions of PPTs and anyone can access the latest version from any device,” says Ravindra Dhawan, Head of IT Infrastructure Platform at M&M. 

- Business continuity: While Teams has been an enabler towards business continuity enterprise wide, in the company’s tractor manufacturing wing, Teams has facilitated meetings with dealers, inspections from auditors, negotiations with suppliers and vendors, and year-end financial roundups by finance teams. Teams is the all-in-one workspace for the entire process. 

- Knowledge sharing: M&M has appended line-of-business apps to Teams, which makes routine tasks and workflows more efficient and seamless. For instance, it has integrated a learning app with Teams and enabled effective training and knowledge sharing. 

Technology evolution is a natural progression. Going forward, M&M has plans to take advantage of continued digital transformation as a means to empower its employees, propel its business to new heights, and deliver exceptional customer service. 

“By focusing on transforming our internal operations through Teams, we have empowered our workforce with everything they need to accomplish their tasks productively and achieve professional growth through an improved work environment. With its rich collaboration experience, Teams has truly transformed the way we work,” concludes Ghosh.

Symphony AzimaAI is building out its predictive equipment model template library by developing additional models that help optimize operations and reduce production losses. ## Introduction

India is the largest producer, consumer and exporter of coffee in the world today, contributing about 48 per cent of the worlds requirement of coffee. As the global demand for coffee is spurring up, it is also throwing up challenges. One of them is maintaining the sustainability of the coffee. Because coffee is a delicate product that can be damaged by high temperature and extreme processing, special care should be taken to ensure products are of top quality.

## Existing Challenges / Problems Faced

Brief description of problem/challenge

- Multiple processes: There were several motors for dry and wet processes which were critical to ensure continuity in production.

- Dependency on manual inspection: Only manual inspection was done for motors, where in one electrician took manual log of all the motor parameters.

- No solution to analyze the health of motors: There was no solution in place to monitor of motor performance and energy consumption to analyze the deterioration of motor health in real time.

- Heavy Production loss:Due to sudden stoppage of critical utility motors. Motor failure was damaging equipment as well.

## What led to the discovery of these problems?

The Coffee manufacturer had suffered huge production loss due to sudden stoppage or unplanned breakdowns. The end user had to maintain huge inventory of utility motors and manpower had to be kept on standby to cater to the sudden break down. Besides there was a pressure to raise the productivity owing to the rising market demand. Lab reports and other mission-critical details like temperature and pressure settings were all manual entries, indicating a strong need to digitize the same.

## Approach to Industry 4.0

What was the overall approach towards adopting Industry 4.0 solution?
Owing to the emerging trends in the manufacturing industry, primarily Industry 4.0, this leading coffee Manufacturer was looking for a solution that would help it in continuously monitoring their mission-critical equipment across the plant and provide real-time information regarding the machine health, variations in equipment parameters like pressure and temperature settings etc., and maintain top quality in their processes and products. The demand for lean and efficient processes with high quality as well as high productivity levels asks for mistake-proof operations and hence this Coffee Manufacturer wanted to digitize, automate and improvise all their existing processes.

- Omron partnered with Prusight Solutions - a leading Industry 4.0 solution provider - and proposed a solution that could facilitate remote monitoring of equipment, reduce maintenance cost and reduce unplanned downtimes by detecting abnormalities in real time.

- The overall turnkey solution was realized using OMRON’s IIoT capable devices like K6CM – the real-time motor condition monitoring device and NX102 - a compact PLC, capable of seamless integratng with both field and IT layer.

- The real time equipment parameters like vibration, temperature and current are captured by K6CM and communicated to NX102 on Ethernet IP which are polled to the server using NX102’s built in database connectivity option eliminating the requirement of a middleware.

- The data from the server is then captured and visualized using interactive dashboard developed by Prusight Solution.

- OMRON’s predictive maintenance solution integrated with Prusight’s capabilities allowed the systems to predict when exactly the equipment might breakdown and sends alerts to the respective teams for corrective measures well within the time frame.

- Lab reports and other mission-critical details like temperature and pressure settings are all digitized to avoid any manual entry in the system, thus reducing errors to virtually zero.

## Challenges faced while implementing the solution

The major challenges that were faced foreseen before implementation of the project were:

- Limited networking option available in the existing machinery.

- Modelling the predictive algorithm to detect abnormalities.

The risks were mitigated by:

- conducting extensive trials to successfully establish connectivity on the existing machinery.

- data analytics on the captured data to arrive at the predictive model.

## Benefits acheived

The benefits of OMRONs industrial IIOT automation solutions provided with Prusight were measurable within just two weeks of implementation, supporting the plant processes involved in coffee production.

- Reduction in error rate :Having implemented the solutions, a reduction of the error rate from 5% to nearly zero has been achieved and the intertwined operations are unraveled.

- Overall productivity increased :by 32% with the data integration from OMRON system linked to Prusights inventory management processes.

- Production costs reduced : by 43%, with more predictable inventory requirements.

- Error rate reduced close to zero : with 46% increase in efficiency owing to digitally optimized processes and data capture.

The solution implementation was done in phases:

- Phase 2:Operators were trained to access the dashboard and export data records and reports.

The human effort to access the critical machinery distributed across plant area was reduced. Manual data recording process was eliminated reducing effort and errors in data.

## Approach to Industry 4.0

With one global quality standard, it also produces for Daimler Trucks’ brands of FUSO, Mercedes-Benz, and Freightliner. Products and parts are exported to more than 50 markets in the Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East. DICV represents an overall investment of more than INR 9,560 crores.

DICV is the only Daimler location worldwide that produces engines, transmissions, trucks and buses at the same site under four brands – BharatBenz, FUSO, Mercedes-Benz and Freightliner. DICV has exported over 35,000 CVs to more than 50 markets globally and also delivered over 5500 CKD kits.

Starting in 2016, DICV assembled the Mercedes-Benz parts from complete knock-down (CKD), a kit of the completely non-assembled parts of a product. DICV also was supplying Fuso truck CKD kits to Kenya for local assembly by a partner, and to a Daimler truck production plant in East London, South Africa.

The CKD exports are sent to Kenya, South Africa, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Malaysia; each country has different requirements and standards – and different parts.

CKD exports are kitted using process modeling in FactoryTalk® ProductionCentre® Manufacturing Execution System (MES), which mistake-proofs the kits by guiding operators and checking the kit automatically. Based on this, local assembly partners consume the CKD kits with full confidence.

Combined with ControlLogix® PLCs, Rockwell Automation® Software along with partner PTC, this custom Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) platform allows employees to now make decisions in real-time to analyze and improve manufacturing productivity.

Before the control room was designed, supervisors and experts on the floor communicated through radio and cell phones, reactively looking at report screens. With the control room, employees become proactive and can prevent issues from affecting production throughput or quality.

## Real Data In Real Time

The addition of a production control room brought the data to the people, so decisions are quicker – improving productivity. With FactoryTalk ProductionCentre, DICV can now:

- Facilitate demand to production and order management.

- Generate serial numbers and build sheet printing for vehicle assembly.

title: Automated system for SSD/DRAM Module Manufacturer for efficient manufacturing process.
writeup:
## About Getech Automation Pte Ltd

Getech designs and manufacture industrial automation machine and equipment under the GETECH brand. These machines are used in the electronics, semiconductor, pharmacy, medical equipment and defence equipment manufacturing industries.

## Case in point: SSD and DRAM Module Manufacturer

This Client is a world leader in innovative memory solutions that transform how the world uses information. They have been instrumental to the world’s most significant technology advancements, delivering optimal memory and storage systems for a broad range of applications. The company is a major manufacturer of memory and storage technologies - DRAM, NAND and NOR technology.

## Existing challenges/ problems faced

- SSD and DRAM Modules are manufactured using SMT (Surface Mount Technology). Post reflow processes are done by operators manually resulting in inconsistent and low product quality.

- Getech was invited to build an automation system to replace the manual processes. Some of the processes are digitized with new network resulting in quality and efficiency improvement.

## Approach to Industry 4.0

- Getech studied the manual processes and designed an automated system to replace them the steps.

- Next challenge was to network the machines and software protocols to exchange data among machines as well as cloud repository servers.

## About Industry 4.0 solution

Getech has developed Robotic Automation Machines (Green icons in below picture) with SECS/GEM software protocols. All the machines are networked with LAN ports. Digital data is instantaneously transferred among the machines and servers. Process is fine-tuned real-time basis. R&D releases vital data through cloud repository server. Machines use latest vital data such as product firmware, and label templates from cloud repository server instantaneously.

Brief description of processes: 

- Reflow is last process in PCBA assembly process.

- AOI (Automatic Optical Inspection) checks for SMT component and process visual defects

- RBM is a depanelizing/routing mechanical process.

- Sorting is a routing quality inspection and sorting process.

- Testing is a functional test process.

- CTO is a Configure to Order process which is downloading the firmware to SSD and labelling.

- Box packing is packing the SSD or DRAM Modules in carton box ready to ship.

All Getech machines update SECS/GEM host machine with machine status such as Idle, Setup, Executing, Pause. Using this data server generate OEE reports. OEE reports helps engineers to focus on improving the process continuously. 

- Sorting machine receives AOI inspection results for every product on real time basis over the network. Sorting machine is integrated with routing inspection process. It uses AOI inspection results and local routing inspection data to sort the products into tray bins.

- RBM machine receives routing inspection results from Sorting machines over network real time basis. RBM machines uses routing inspection results and compensate routing machine recipe instantaneously. This real time feedback helped to improved consistent product quality and Cpk of depanelizing process.

- CTO machine uses latest firmware and label templates from cloud repository. Even though R&D is in different geographical location the product produced is with latest firmware and label templates. Customer R&D releases firmware and label temple templates as when needed through cloud repository servers. No manual intervention is needed.

## Challenges faced while implementing the solution

Few challenges in implementing these solutions.

- Each machine UPH (units per hour), Cost and Size are critical parameters to achieve acceptable ROI. SECS/GEM protocols are new to PCBA (printed circuit board assembly) process. It has taken lots of software designers time in developing specific protocols. As the server infrastructure is provided by customer, customer support was key in implementing networked processes. Understanding manual process and digitization formats were critical.

- Development machines were done in phased manner to reduce the risk of each project. First proof-of-concepts developed and tested for key features. Then actual machines were developed.

## Benefits achieved

- Scalable processes. Best product yields and product quality

- Consistent process.

- OEE monitoring and improving

- Affordable machine prices to meet customer ROI targets

[https://www.linkedin.com/posts/getech-automation-pt-ltd_issue-14-q3-2021-i40-today-activity-6849306518479753216-wKkY](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/getech-automation-pt-ltd_issue-14-q3-2021-i40-today-activity-6849306518479753216-wKkY)
